correctness.rationale: For two agents and mutually independent Bernoulli(p_j) values on each agent-good pair, per-agent EF1 failure is explicitly enumerable, and cross-agent events multiply. With m=3 an ex-ante EF partition can be parametrized by (x+y,x,y), and balanced singleton probability exceeds alternatives by y² and x²; empty-bundle allocations cannot improve. For m=4 with p=(eps,1/3,2/3,1/3+eps), A={1,3}|{2,4} is exactly ex-ante EF while B={3}|{1,2,4} is not. Computing A and B EF1 probabilities from independent Bernoulli vectors gives difference eps*(19-652eps+48eps²-36eps³)/729; its cubic is strictly decreasing over (0,1/3), with unique positive crossover ~0.0292025. At eps=1/60 the exact excess is 5431/29160000. Integer subset-sum weights (1,20,40,21) confirm A and its complement are all ex-ante EF partitions. Independently computed two-agent joint probabilities by finite exact Fraction enumeration (A=27909869/29160000, B=10339/10800) and verified gap and polynomial simplification. General m<=3 proof is analytic.
residual_risks: The threshold describes only A-vs-B comparison, not a global optimum for all eps. Proof of m<=3 covers ex-ante EF where it exists.

evidence: Existing exact EF optimality has no readable EF1 counterpart; full shared-value EF1 theorem requires a single realized value common to all agents, unlike this agent-specific independent sampling; fair-allocation lotteries with fixed utilities randomize allocation instead.

evidence: Record3 varies probabilities by agent with all goods identical within agent, so any two-two allocation is ex-ante EF, and cannot specialize to distinct p_j=(eps,1/3,2/3,1/3+eps) within each agent. Record4 instead keeps agent marginals identical per good and constructs a non-expected-EF superior EF1 allocation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A common four-good horizon is not theorem equivalence; neither heterogeneous parameter axis implies the other. The exact r=3 boundary is an independent nontrivial claim.

evidence: Ex-ante EF is equality of expected subset sums, while realized EF1 is at most one valued good removed; the objective concerns probability over independent agent-good randomness with varying p_j. Igarashi-Oh known results concern exact EF, which is strictly stronger event and different optimization.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Not equivalent to randomizing an allocation itself, or to per-agent iid parameters. Here both agents have identical marginal p_j on each good, but values remain independent across agents, so neither shared-realization theorem nor global iid symmetry applies.

value.rationale: A concrete smallest-good-number counterexample disproves a natural probability-optimality extrapolation from ex-ante expected fairness to ex-post EF1. The sharp analytic parameter window and exact unique expected-fair partition make the witness robust and reproducible. Its small numerical gain is not the sole motivation; the precise m<=3 versus m=4 boundary is the mathematical point.
residual_risks: Scope limited to two-agent binary independent item-value model, not general fair allocation.

limitations: Four-good polynomial threshold compares named A and B; global optimum over all allocations not classified for every epsilon.
